brief: The town has a year and thirteen trees that have never heard of it. drawTree draws the courtyard linden; drawLaneTree draws four street trees (TREE_PITS), four plaza trees (PLAZA_PITS) and four orchard trees (ORCHARD, fruit:1). Every one is sized on maturity(), which pinned at day 8, and filled from a hard-coded array of summer greens. So in deep winter the beds are correctly turned earth, the sun correctly sets at 18.30, and thirteen trees stand in full leaf above it. Make the canopies read `warmth`: bare or nearly bare in winter, thin and light in spring, full and dark in summer, turning in autumn — the orchard's existing fruit:1 flag is the natural place to hang blossom and then fruit. And fix the falling leaves while you are there: the `leaves` spawner is gated on `day>=4 || gusty` and scaled on richness(), a ramp that pinned at day 16, so leaves fall out of those permanently green trees at the same rate in July and January. Put the fall on the season, peaking in autumn. This is the single loudest thing a thirty-second viewer sees wrong, it is in the wide shot, and it is the same contradiction in four domains at once.
successLooksLike: Four wide shots at the same hour, one per season, are unmistakably four different times of year from the trees alone — and the winter one has no full green canopy anywhere in it. Leaves fall in autumn and hardly at all in midsummer.
avoid: Do not make the trees change SIZE with the season — maturity() sizes them, and a tree that grows and shrinks every 24 real minutes reads as a bug, not a year. Do not go fully bare and stay there; winter should keep the orchard's structure and the linden's silhouette. And this is the biggest thing drawn in the frame: LAW says the largest gated draw is the pop, so cross the seasons on a ramp and prove it with a region-cropped filmstrip, not the whole-frame mean, which will be loud about the sky regardless.
